title: Waking up
hook: praise to Allah who gave us life after death, and to Him is the return (Bukhari)
tomorrow: Dadi's at the door with her cane, going out alone. what does she say?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a hundred glorifications: sins as light as the sea's foam, and a few phrases that outweighed a morning. Like the sea's foam. Today, the very first words of a day.
screen: `LIKE THE SEA'S FOAM.` → `THE FIRST WORDS OF A DAY.`

segments.voice: Phones have a sleep mode: screen dark, still running, waiting for a touch. The first words the Prophet ﷺ said on waking go much further than that. In Sahih al-Bukhari: praise to Allah, who gave us life after He had given us death, and to Him is the return. Gave us death? Nobody died last night. Everyone just slept. So why would a morning line call sleep a kind of dying?
screen: `SLEEP MODE.` → `LIFE AFTER DEATH, EVERY MORNING?` → `NOBODY DIED. EVERYONE SLEPT.`

segments.voice: The answer is in the Qur'an itself. Surah az-Zumar says that God takes the souls at the time of their death, and takes the souls that have not died, in their sleep. He keeps the ones whose death is decreed, and sends the others back, for a set term. Sleep, in that verse, is a small letting-go. Each night the soul is held, and each morning, for now, it's given back. That's the puzzle solved, and the detail to tell a friend tonight: in this tradition, waking up is a small rehearsal of rising again. The same hadith gives the night its own line, said lying down: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. Put the two together and a day has a shape. Handed over at night; handed back in the morning. The waking line's last word is nushur, the return, a word the Qur'an also uses for the raising of the dead. So a morning isn't only a new day. It's a life given back without being asked for, before you've done a single thing to earn it. Alive again.
screen: `TAKEN IN SLEEP, SENT BACK.` · `A SMALL REHEARSAL.` · `IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND LIVE.` · `NUSHUR: THE RETURN.` · then, large: `ALIVE AGAIN.`

segments.voice: If there's water near you, take one slow sip, the way you might first thing in the morning, and notice it reach you. Then say, aloud or inside, the waking line or its meaning: praise to Allah, who gave us life after death, and to Him is the return. If you don't pray, simply notice that this morning was handed to you; you didn't make it.
screen: `ONE SLOW SIP.` · `THE WAKING LINE.` · `THIS MORNING WAS HANDED TO YOU.`

segments.voice: Waking up: the first line of the day, praise for life given back after sleep, with the return to Him in its last word.
For the morning: alive again, each day handed back to you, not earned by you. Waking, explained.

howItsDone: Muslims say this line on waking, often before getting out of bed, and say 'in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live' when lying down to sleep.

an-nushur for the raising of the dead: e.g. 35:9 ('such is the resurrection'); 67:15 ('unto Him is the resurrection'). Confirm.
